Mike Mazzei

Republican candidate for Governor, Oklahoma · Open seat

Businessman; founder and CEO of an investment management firm in Tulsa; former state senator

Mike Mazzei is a Tulsa businessman. He served in the Oklahoma State Senate from 2004 to 2016 and was Gov. Kevin Stitt's Secretary of Budget from 2019 to 2020. He came in first or second in the nine-candidate Republican primary on June 16, 2026, then beat Attorney General Gentner Drummond by about 2,000 votes in the August 25 runoff to become the Republican nominee for governor.

Where Mazzei stands

Income tax
Proposes a three-phase plan to eliminate Oklahoma's individual income tax within six years. He says this would help the state compete for higher-paying jobs.
Property tax
Proposes eliminating property taxes for seniors 65 and older and for veterans.
State spending
Proposes a state Department of Government Efficiency and an Office of State Finance and Fiscal Responsibility to cut waste and fraud and to help offset revenue lost from tax cuts.
Education
Supports hiring a statewide literacy director, more transparency for parents, higher teacher pay and more pathways into teaching. Supports school choice.
School funding
In the Oct. 1 debate, he argued against putting more money into what he called a dysfunctional system without changes to it.
Transgender students in school sports and bathrooms
Supports keeping boys out of girls' sports and girls' bathrooms in schools.
Inola aluminum smelter
Supports the planned aluminum smelter in Inola.
OETA public television
Says he believes OETA can compete in the private marketplace. He did not commit to reauthorizing it, saying it depends on what the Legislature does.
Health care, insurance and infrastructure
Lists rural health care, insurance costs, roads and bridges, data centers and tribal-state cooperation among the areas where he would propose changes.
Foreign land ownership
Has called for limiting foreign ownership of Oklahoma land, particularly by Chinese companies.

Background

  • Oklahoma State Senate, District 25 (2004–2016); chaired the Senate Finance Committee
  • Oklahoma Secretary of Budget under Gov. Kevin Stitt (2019–2020)
  • Entered the 2022 Oklahoma State Treasurer race in August 2021, withdrew the next month
  • Founder of The Financial Coach Inc.; chairman and CEO of Trinity Strategic Wealth (Tulsa)
  • B.A. in government and politics, George Mason University; attended the College for Financial Planning
  • Won the Republican gubernatorial runoff on Aug. 25, 2026
